title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of innovation and regulatory maneuvers as startups challenge established norms and government budgets expand. Meanwhile, the hypersonic program continues to stumble, and new partnerships are forming to enhance satellite capabilities.

themes.title: Startups vs. Established Players
themes.body: A new startup is shaking up the satellite industry’s multi-orbit strategy, suggesting that the old playbook might be due for a rewrite. This could lead to a more competitive landscape as traditional players scramble to adapt.

themes.title: Government Funding Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a strong commitment to enhancing national security through space. This influx of cash could catalyze innovation and partnerships across the sector.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle program has once again slipped, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the program's viability and the broader implications for U.S. defense capabilities.

themes.title: Strategic Partnerships Forming
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, showcasing a trend of collaboration among defense tech firms. Such alliances could reshape the competitive landscape as they pool resources and expertise.
